import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

<Aside type="caution" title="The ported run-loop is now RETIRED (2026-06-06)">
This is a **historical handoff doc**. The TS run-loop this port produced
(`main-loop.ts`, `bin/run.ts`, `pre-loop.ts`, the checkpoints/snapshots/dispatches
cluster) was retired and archived to `libs/papercusp/_retired/orchestrator-run-loop/`
(plan `archive-legacy-orchestrator-deadcode-2026-06-06`; git tag
`legacy-orchestrator-run-loop-retired-2026-06-06`) — superseded by the **DBOS
durable pipeline** (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`).

Parts of the port were deliberately kept LIVE rather than moved: `invoke.ts`,
`lanes.ts`, the worker chunk-loop (`worker-chunk-loop.ts` /
`chunk-loop-driver.ts`), `cost-cap.ts`, and `decision-parse.ts` all remain in
the `@papercusp/orchestrator` package (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/`)
and are **consumed** by the DBOS pipeline via `@papercusp/orchestrator` imports
(e.g. `parseDecision`, `parseDecisionFor`, `DECISION_VERBS` in
`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`). They do **not** live inside the
`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/` directory.

The `papercusp-orchestrate` bin and the `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR`
fall-through described below no longer exist. Note also that `bash run.sh` itself
was deleted entirely (2026-05-30): the TS path became the canonical, only
main-loop driver well before this retirement, and `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=0`
is now a warning-only no-op, **not** a working bash fallback. The body below —
describing `run.sh` as the live fall-through target and the flag as opt-in — is
historical and no longer accurate.
</Aside>

## Why this exists

The autonomous-harness orchestrator was historically a 2,122-line bash script (`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/run.sh`). The desktop app needs to drop the bash prereq for Windows users (Git for Windows is currently required to run the loop). A TypeScript port of `run.sh` achieves that without losing Claude Max subscription support — the port keeps the agent CLI (`omp -p` by default, `claude -p` opt-in) as a child-process spawn rather than switching to the SDK.

<Aside type="caution" title="Hard constraint for handoff">
Do **not** swap the agent CLI (`omp -p` or `claude -p`) for `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. Both CLIs handle Claude Max auth via the user's Claude Code session (omp via Meridian's SDK-bridge, claude directly); the SDK route requires API keys and breaks Max users. The whole point of the port is to drop bash, not the CLI layer.
</Aside>

## Where it lives

New package `@papercusp/orchestrator` at `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/` (in the `papercupai/papercusp` submodule). Feature-flagged via `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=1` — currently opt-in. The CLI entry `bin/run.ts` handles the flag and falls through to bash for any decision branch the TS port doesn't yet cover.

## Cutover gate (when to flip the default flag)

Stage 5a is now ✅ — the TS orchestrator covers every run.sh code path. Remaining cutover gate items:

1. End-to-end run against `papercup/sheets-clone` validates identical observable behavior to bash for at least one full mission cycle (PLAN → WORKER → VALIDATOR → DONE).
2. Cost-cap edge cases verified: `total_cost_usd` accumulation matches bash's python heredoc within 1¢; soft-warn fires once; over-cap exits 6.
3. Validate competition-mode end-to-end against a real harness (the unit suite covers the state machine; an integration run is the final check).
4. Flip `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=1` default-on in `apps/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` spawn.

## For the handoff agent (after Stage 5a)

Stage 5a is ✅ now (commit `c84f3b0` on `papercupai/papercusp`). The next concrete task is **the cutover end-to-end validation**:

1. Pick a coding harness (e.g. `~/sheets-clone`) and a clean state. Run a single mission with `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=1 ~/autonomous-harness/run.sh` (or invoke the orchestrator package's bin directly).
2. Compare against the same mission run with the flag unset (bash). Verify: same features land in `passed`, same logs end up in `<stateDir>/logs/`, same total cost, same `notify_event done` payload.
3. Run a parallel-lane harness (config: `parallelWorkers.max=2 + branchIso`) on a feature that's quick to validate. Confirm the second worker's lane shows up in `<stateDir>/lanes.json` and the validator drains both before running.
4. Run a competition-mode harness (config: `parallelWorkers.max=2 + parallelWorkers.mode=competition + branchIso + useWorktrees`) on a feature with a 2-of-2 lane fixture. Confirm both worktrees get spawned, validator emits `COMPETITION_WINNER lane-1`, the winner branch merges cleanly, the loser worktree gets removed.
5. After all three modes pass: edit `apps/papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` to default `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=1` in the spawn env. Tag `desktop-v0.0.2-test1` and verify the bundle still works.
6. Add the `apps/papercusp-desktop/sidecar/` build to NOT ship `harness/run.sh` once the TS path is the canonical entry — saves ~2k lines of bash from the bundle. (Optional polish; leave for later.)

Auto-memory at `~/.claude/projects/-tmp/memory/project_desktop_app_build.md` has the full pitfall log from desktop-v0.0.1 bring-up (8 test iterations to ship) — read before tag-and-shipping desktop-v0.0.2.
